newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT seeks exemption from new proxy rule.
newsitem.headline: PLDT seeks exemption from new proxy rule.

text.p: The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) had asked the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to exempt it from the new proxy rule for its 1997 stockholders' meeting scheduled in April.

The SEC has imposed stricter rules on proxy votes gathering and voting including uniform proxy statements and forms to be approved and issued by SEC. The PLDT stockholders' meeting is scheduled on April 16.

"We anticipate that due to the number of its stockholders, it would be very difficult, if not impossible, for PLDT to comply, with respect to this year's scheduled annual stockholders meeting, with the requirement of furnishing each of its stockholders with the required proxy statement (accompanied by the annual report to shareholders) within the prescribed period," PLDT senior executive vice president Enrique Perez said in a letter.
He said many PLDT shareholders lived overseas.
Perez added the requirement of listing of all nominated directors would not be feasible as the government which controls five of the eleven seats are made usually close to the meeting date.

"We wish to emphasise that this request is only for this year's annual stockholders' meeting since we anticipate that PLDT would be in a better position to comply with the said requirements ... for the 1998 annual stockholders' meeting," he added.
